tldr:
The note proves the constant-factor sample frontier for discovering positive stratum CATEs from the original iid observational records:
\[
N(p,s,\delta)=p\max\{\delta^{-2}L,\delta^{-7/2}\sqrt L\},\qquad N_e(p,s,\delta)=p\delta^{-2}L,\qquad L=1+\log(p/s).
\]
The second frontier supplies the entire true propensity vector on the identical primitive class. The two unknown-propensity branches meet at \(L=\delta^{-3}\). Explicit total computable selectors have whole-class FDR at most \(1/10\) for every finite sample size and uniform expected recall at least \(4/5\) at the stated upper budgets. Matching converses cover every randomized subset procedure in the original fixed-total-sample experiment and every augmented procedure for the oracle bound. The proof retains the full sparsity logarithm and both random-occupancy regimes. The target is the sign of each causal stratum mean effect; potential-outcome coupling remains unrestricted.
gap: Beneficiary-FDR procedures and CATE level-set minimax theory address neighboring decisions. Published sparse-sequence boundaries do not evaluate that causal experiment.
